supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

derivations.claim:
For $i=1,2$, [F1] and [A1] give $W_{\omega_i}-H_\mu\in C^\infty(U\times U)$ on each prescribed neighborhood $U$. Their difference is therefore smooth:
$$(W_{\omega_1}-H_\mu)-(W_{\omega_2}-H_\mu)=W_{\omega_1}-W_{\omega_2}.$$
Since $D_{ab}$ is finite order and maps smooth biscalars to smooth tensor-valued functions, its application to this difference is smooth near the diagonal and has a coincidence limit.

Apply [F1] separately to both states and subtract. The common $C_{ab}$ cancels, and linearity of $D_{ab}$ gives
$$T^{\mathrm{ren}}_{ab}[g,\omega_1]-T^{\mathrm{ren}}_{ab}[g,\omega_2]=\lim_{y\to x}\left(D_{ab}(W_{\omega_1}-H_\mu)-D_{ab}(W_{\omega_2}-H_\mu)\right)=\lim_{y\to x}D_{ab}(W_{\omega_1}-W_{\omega_2}),$$
where existence of the final limit follows from step 1.1.

If a common state-independent local curvature tensor $K_{ab}[g]$ is added to both prescriptions, their difference becomes $(T^{\mathrm{ren}}[g,\omega_1]+K[g])-(T^{\mathrm{ren}}[g,\omega_2]+K[g])$, which equals the difference in step 2.1 by cancellation. This establishes only independence of common local additions to the difference, not independence of either absolute stress tensor.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g)$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented, time-oriented,
globally hyperbolic smooth Lorentzian four-manifold without boundary, with
signature $(-,+,+,+)$. An orientation is a smooth choice of orientation in
each tangent space, and a time orientation selects the future timelike cone.
Use the causal-curve and $J^\pm$ conventions of
[[def-qftx-wavefront-hadamard]]: a future causal curve is a continuous map
$c:I\to M$ on a real interval $I$, piecewise $C^1$ on each compact subinterval
with finitely many pieces there, and with nonzero future-directed causal
tangent on each smooth piece; a past causal curve uses the opposite cone. If
an endpoint belongs to $I$, its value is the continuous endpoint value. Then
$J^+(p)$ consists of $p$ and every $q$ reached by a future causal curve
$c:[a,b]\to M$, $a<b$, with $c(a)=p$ and $c(b)=q$, and
$J^-(p)=\{q:p\in J^+(q)\}$. Strong causality means every point has
arbitrarily small neighborhoods that each causal curve meets in a connected
parameter interval. Global hyperbolicity means strong causality and compact
causal diamonds $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$. Fix a real scalar Klein-Gordon operator
$P=-g^{ab}\nabla_a\nabla_b+V$, where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection
and $V$ is a prescribed smooth real scalar of dimension $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ in
length coordinates. Use the canonical field length degree
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ used for the framework's free scalar field, so its
two-point distribution and subtraction kernel have length degree
$\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. Supply the free-field $*$-algebra $\mathcal A_P$ and its
real test-function smearing map $\Phi:C_c^\infty(M;\mathbb R)\to\mathcal A_P$;
smearing uses $d\mathrm{vol}_g$. This is model input, not a field-algebra
construction claim. In the massless minimally coupled collapse
specialization, [[post-tgrx-free-collapse-scattering]] specifies bosonic
Fock quantization, the smeared field operators, and the positive normalized
state convention. A **state** $\omega$ is a positive normalized linear
functional on $\mathcal A_P$, so $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ and $\omega(1)=1$.
Its two-point distribution $W_\omega\in\mathcal D'(M\times M)$, in the
test-density convention, is defined by the pairings
$W_\omega(f,h)=\omega(\Phi(f)\Phi(h))$ for compactly supported smooth real
tests $f,h$, extended complex linearly. Require
$P_xW_\omega=P_yW_\omega=0$ and
$\operatorname{WF}(W_\omega)=\mathcal C_g^+$, where $\mathcal C_g^+$ consists
of pairs $(x,\xi;y,-\zeta)$ with nonzero future-null covectors $\xi,\zeta$
that are equal at a coincident point or are the metric-dual tangents, with a
common positive scale, along one nonconstant future-directed null geodesic;
the two base points need not be ordered along that geodesic. This is the
positive-frequency Hadamard convention in [[def-qftx-wavefront-hadamard]],
whose definition fixes this relation without a base-point order.
$\operatorname{WF}$ records nonzero cotangent directions in which localized
Fourier transforms fail rapid decay. The
framework's massless, minimally coupled collapse scalar is one
specialization; its Schwarzschild and scattering assumptions are not imposed
on this general contract.

For each open convex normal neighborhood $U\subset M$ (an open set such that
for every $p\in U$ the exponential map at $p$ restricts to a diffeomorphism
from a star-shaped open neighborhood of $0\in T_pM$ onto $U$), supply a
locally covariant Hadamard singular bidistribution $H_\mu$ for $P$. The scale
$\mu>0$ is fixed and has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. “Hadamard singular
bidistribution” here means the prescribed local, state-independent singular
part determined by $(g,P,\mu)$, with
$W_\omega-H_\mu\in C^\infty(U\times U)$. The parametrix pieces, the
bidifferential operators below, and their resulting coincident values must be
compatible on overlaps. This is supplied data: the definition proves no
parametrix construction or general existence theorem.

Supply a finite-order bidifferential operator $D_{ab}(x,y)$ which maps a
smooth biscalar on $U\times U$ to a smooth covariant symmetric two-tensor at
$x$; any coefficient bitensors and parallel transports needed to define its
indices are part of the supplied operator. Also supply a smooth, symmetric,
state-independent local curvature tensor $C_{ab}[g;\mu,\mathbf c]$, where
$\mathbf c$ is the fixed list of finite renormalization conditions. “Local”
means determined by the values of $g$, $P$, and their derivatives at the
point, through finitely many curvature contractions; it has no state or
distant-geometry dependence. Require local covariance: whenever
$\psi:(M,g)\to(M',g')$ is a smooth embedding with $\psi^*g'=g$, preserves the
time orientation, and has causally convex image (every causal curve segment
in $M'$ with endpoints in the image stays in the image), the assigned local
prescription on $(M,g)$ is the pullback of the one on $(M',g')$. Require
conservation,
$\nabla^aT^{\mathrm{ren}}_{ab}=0$, with the index raised using $g^{ab}$.

Define the renormalized stress tensor by
$$T^{\mathrm{ren}}_{ab}[g,\omega](x):=\lim_{y\to x}D_{ab}(x,y)\bigl(W_\omega-H_\mu\bigr)(x,y)+C_{ab}[g;\mu,\mathbf c](x).$$
The limit is taken inside a convex normal neighborhood. It exists because
$W_\omega-H_\mu$ is smooth and $D_{ab}$ has finite order. In SI units and
length coordinates $x^0=ct$, the normalization of $D_{ab}$ is part of the
chosen scalar-field prescription and its output, as well as $C_{ab}$, has
stress-energy units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. No pointwise product of the
singular distributions $W_\omega$ and $H_\mu$ is taken.

derivations.claim: Under [A1], apply the exact diagnostic formula and bound in [F1]. They depend only on the ODE mass history and constants in that ODE; neither contains a spacetime metric $g$, state $\omega$, curvature tensor, or renormalized stress tensor.

By [F1], the formula and upper bound use only the scalar history $M(t_\infty)$ and ODE constants; no metric, state, curvature tensor, or stress tensor occurs in them. Thus step 1.1 establishes only a bound for this scalar diagnostic.

By [F2], the residual $\mathcal R_{ab}[g,\omega]$ depends on a supplied metric, its curvature tensors, the selected state and the renormalized stress prescription. These are additional inputs and are not quantities in the ODE diagnostic of step 1.1.

The ODE diagnostic in step 1.1 supplies no state or renormalized-stress estimate for the residual in step 2.2, and neither [F1] nor [F2] supplies a relation that bounds the candidate metric and state in terms of that scalar diagnostic. Hence no component estimate for $\mathcal R_{ab}$ follows from the ODE bound alone. Obtaining one would require an additional metric/state relation and curvature/stress estimates. This is a limit of the stated inputs; it asserts neither an unbounded residual nor an instability.
